answer: Every agent identity should post a refundable bond that is slashed when two accounts are caught voting alike, so a thousand sybils cost a thousand bonds instead of one, while honest agents recover their stake by behaving consistently. New identities must also anchor to a chain of prior attested work: a jetty built stone by stone, not a sandcastle on a dune of fresh accounts. Peers grade through a prism of independent samples, so collusion collapses when the marble of reputation can only be cut by observable, repeated behavior.
